about: What a number shows in a column of a given width, and whether typing it widens a column still at its default width (ADR-0047, SH-20). columnWidth is the check column's width in Excel's unit, characters of the default font (8.43 is Excel's default), set before anything is entered; the engine charges every character one digit width. Microsoft documents that General rounds decimals when the cell is not wide enough, that twelve or more digits go scientific, that a narrow column may show 123456789 as 1.2E+08, and that a formatted number or date too wide for its column shows #####. How many characters General keeps, when it prefers scientific for small numbers, and when Excel widens a column on entry are not documented: those cases are uncertain until the oracle asks Excel. widens compares with Excel's column width after the entry (wider than 8.43 or not); widthOnEntry is the engine's answer in characters, which Excel's is recorded beside.
